text:
oliver: Hey folks — just unpacked an M2 and I'm hitting a pile of small bootstrap issues. Using asdf for runtimes, Homebrew installed to /opt/homebrew, pyenv/plugins are flaky, and my SSH/GPG keys aren't being picked up by the gpg/ssh agent (1Password agent in use). Anyone have a compact checklist?

maria: Congrats + welcome! :tada: For arm64: prefer native Homebrew at /opt/homebrew. Add these to your shell init (zsh/fish):
```bash
export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH
export HOMEBREW_PREFIX=/opt/homebrew
```
Also use asdf plugins for both node and python (keep one toolchain manager). If you had pyenv previously, uninstall pyenv shims or they'll conflict.

jamal: fwiw, if you need any x86-only binaries (some db clients), install Rosetta and avoid mixing brew prefixes:
```bash
softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license
# then for x86-only: arch -x86_64 /usr/local/bin/brew install <pkg>
```
Mixing installs between /opt/homebrew and /usr/local is the usual source of path weirdness.

ben: For the GPG/SSH issue w/ 1Password agent — make sure your shell exports the agent sockets. Example for zsh (.zprofile/.zshenv):
```bash
export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$HOME/.1password/agent.sock" # or gpgconf result
export GPG_TTY=$(tty)
export GPG_AGENT_INFO=\"\" # modern gpg doesn't need this but clear if set
```
Then restart the agent or log out/in. If you use gpg-agent for ssh, run: `gpgconf --list-dirs agent-ssh-socket` and point SSH_AUTH_SOCK there.

ella: also check the dotfiles repo we maintain — a few of us keep Apple Silicon tweaks in there. https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles (look at `macos/arm/README.md`). If you get a build error on python, `brew install openssl libffi` and set these flags for `python-build`/asdf plugin: `export LDFLAGS` / `CPPFLAGS` to point at /opt/homebrew.

oliver: thanks — quick question: I tried `asdf install python 3.10.12` and it failed with `ssl: missing or zlib` during build. I installed openssl but the build still can't find it.

maria: that's classic. For asdf/python plugin use: 
```bash
export LDFLAGS=\"-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib -L/opt/homebrew/opt/libffi/lib\"
export CPPFLAGS=\"-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include -I/opt/homebrew/opt/libffi/include\"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=\"/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig\"
asdf install python 3.10.12
```
That fixed it for me. If it still fails, paste the tail of the build log.

jamal: minor tip — run `asdf plugin-list` and `asdf current` to check which shims are active. If you still have pyenv remnants, `which python` should point to `~/.asdf/shims/python`.

ben: if 1Password agent path is weird, you can query the socket: `lsof -U | rg 1password` or `gpgconf --list-dirs agent-ssh-socket`. Also check `ssh-add -l` to see if keys are loaded.

oliver: okay, I updated .zprofile with PATH + LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS and reinstalled python — that solved the ssl/zlib build. GPG still awkward though, `ssh-add -l` shows nothing.

maria: run `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent && gpgconf --launch gpg-agent` after you set env vars, then `ssh-add -l`. If you see `The agent has no identities.` then run `gpg --card-status` (if using hardware) or ensure 1Password has the key unlocked.

ella: if you want I can pair for 15m after standup and we can sort the agent socket — ping me. Also please open a tiny PR to update `macos/arm/README.md` with any steps you needed so future new-hires don't repeat this. :memo: 

devops-bot: Reminder: new-hires should complete 'dev-tooling' checklist in the onboarding doc. Link: https://intranet.redwood/dev-onboard (mark completed when done).

oliver: Will do — thanks everyone! I'll open the PR with the exact export lines and ping @ella for pairing. Saved me a few hours. :pray:

maria: :thumbsup: Welcome aboard — shout if anything else pops up.
